info.new_law.title: The new 2026 law
info.new_law.what_changed.title: What did the new law change?
info.new_law.what_changed.body:
Since 2026 a new law applies to workers from outside the European Union: Emergency Ordinance (OUG) no. 32/2026. The most important changes:
• The work permit (aviz de muncă) no longer exists. The agency or employer submits a “single application” on the WorkinRomania.gov.ro platform.
• In the first 6 months you cannot leave for another employer on your own initiative.
• If you came through an agency, for up to 2 years you can change employer only through the same agency.
• Your salary is paid only into your bank account.
• The employer must organise a Romanian language course for you.
• Rent for accommodation provided by the employer cannot be more than 25% of your net salary.
Different rules apply to citizens of the Republic of Moldova, Ukraine and Serbia.
info.new_law.what_changed.step1: Read the questions about your contract, pay and changing jobs.
info.new_law.what_changed.step2: If you came to Romania before August 2026, also read the question about the rules for you.
info.new_law.single_application.title: Does the work permit still exist? What is the “single application”?
info.new_law.single_application.body: The work permit (aviz de muncă) no longer exists. Now the placement agency or the authorised employer fills in one application, called a “single application”, on the WorkinRomania.gov.ro platform. Based on it you get the long-stay visa for work (D/AM2) and then the single permit, which is your residence and work permit. Extending your permit and changing employer are also done through a single application.
info.new_law.single_application.step1: Ask the agency or employer to tell you when they submitted the single application and what answer they received.
info.new_law.single_application.step2: Keep a copy of your employment contract and, if you came through an agency, of the placement contract.
info.new_law.single_application.step3: After the extension is approved, book an appointment within 10 days at the General Inspectorate for Immigration for your new permit.
info.new_law.employer_types.title: Registered or authorised employer: what is the difference?
info.new_law.employer_types.body:
To hire foreign workers, an employer must be listed on the WorkinRomania.gov.ro platform.
• A registered employer can hire you only through an authorised placement agency. In this case you also sign a placement contract between you, the employer and the agency.
• An authorised employer is a large company (at least 50 employees) that can hire you directly, without an agency.
Exception: if you got your right to work under the old law, your new employer can hire you directly, without an agency.
info.new_law.employer_types.step1: Ask the employer whether it is registered or authorised and ask for proof.
info.new_law.check_agency.title: How do I check that an agency is allowed to place foreign workers?
info.new_law.check_agency.body: Only authorised agencies can place foreign workers in Romania. They are listed in the Register of placement agencies for foreigners on the WorkinRomania.gov.ro platform. An authorised agency is not allowed to ask you for money: it is paid for the placement only by the employer.
info.new_law.check_agency.step1: Search for the agency’s name on WorkinRomania.gov.ro.
info.new_law.check_agency.step2: If the agency is not listed or asks you for money, do not pay and ask for help.
info.new_law.check_agency.step3: Keep the messages and proof of any payment.
info.contract_pay.title: Contract and pay
info.contract_pay.contract.title: Your contract
info.contract_pay.contracts_needed.title: Which contracts must I receive?
info.contract_pay.contracts_needed.body:
You must have a written individual employment contract. If you came through an agency, you also sign a placement contract between you, the employer and the agency.
The contracts must clearly show your job, gross and net salary, working hours, overtime pay and holidays. They must also say whether the employer provides accommodation, transport or meals, and who pays for them.
The placement contract must also include the contact details of the authorities where you can complain: the Labour Inspection, Immigration, the Police, ANITP and ANOFM.
info.contract_pay.contracts_needed.step1: Ask for a copy of each contract. The employer must give it to you before you start work.
info.contract_pay.contracts_needed.step2: Read the contract before you sign. Do not sign documents you do not understand.
info.contract_pay.contracts_needed.step3: Take clear photos of every page and keep them.
info.contract_pay.contract_language.titl: Must the contract be in a language I understand?
info.contract_pay.contract_language.body: Yes. The employment contract must be in Romanian and in your language or in an international language you understand (for example, English). The same applies to the placement contract. An employer who makes the contract only in Romanian can be fined 6,000 lei for each contract. Workplace safety training must also be given in a language you understand.
info.contract_pay.contract_language.step: If you received the contract only in Romanian, ask in writing (for example, on WhatsApp) for a version in your language or in English.
If you do not get it, you can complain to the Labour Inspection.
info.contract_pay.reges_check.title: How do I find out if I am officially registered as an employee?
info.contract_pay.reges_check.body: Every employment contract must be entered in the electronic register of employees (REGES-ONLINE) at the latest on the day before you start work. If you are not registered, your work is not legal and you may have problems with your residence permit. The start date in REGES matters: the 6-month and 2-year periods are counted from it.
info.contract_pay.reges_check.step1: Ask the employer in writing for a certificate with your data from the register. They must give it to you within 15 working days.
info.contract_pay.reges_check.step2: When you leave the employer, you must receive a certificate and an extract from the register.
info.contract_pay.reges_check.step3: If the employer refuses, you can complain to the Labour Inspection.
info.contract_pay.pay.title: Pay and costs
info.contract_pay.minimum_wage.title: What is the minimum wage?
info.contract_pay.minimum_wage.body: Since 1 July 2026, the gross minimum wage in Romania is 4,325 lei per month for full-time work. You receive about 2,699 lei “in hand” (net). From the gross salary, the pension contribution (25%), the health contribution (10%) and income tax (10%) are deducted. Your employer may not pay you less than a Romanian worker for the same work. In some sectors, for example construction, the minimum wage is higher.
info.contract_pay.minimum_wage.step1: Check the gross and net salary in your contract.
info.contract_pay.minimum_wage.step2: Ask for your payslip every month and keep it.
info.contract_pay.minimum_wage.step3: If you receive less than your contract says, use “I have a problem” in the app to send a complaint to the Labour Inspection.
info.contract_pay.cash_payment.title: Can I be paid in cash?
info.contract_pay.cash_payment.body: No. Under the new law, your employer must pay your salary into your bank account. A bank can open an account for you based on your long-stay work visa or your residence permit. Your salary is paid at least once a month, on the date written in your contract.
info.contract_pay.cash_payment.step1: Open a bank account in your own name if you do not have one.
info.contract_pay.cash_payment.step2: Never give anyone your bank card or PIN.
info.contract_pay.cash_payment.step3: If the employer pays you in cash or does not pay you on time, keep evidence (messages, photos) and complain to the Labour Inspection.
info.contract_pay.accommodation_rent.tit: How much can accommodation from my employer cost?
info.contract_pay.accommodation_rent.bod: If your employer provides accommodation and charges you rent, the rent cannot be more than 25% of your net salary. The job offer and the contract must clearly say whether you get accommodation and meals, under what conditions and who pays. Nothing may be deducted from your salary except in the cases provided by law. For seasonal workers, rent cannot be automatically deducted from the salary.
info.contract_pay.accommodation_rent.ste: Check in your contract whether accommodation is free or paid, and how much it costs.
Do the maths: rent cannot be more than a quarter of your net salary.
If you pay more, keep the evidence and ask for help.
info.contract_pay.fees.title: Can the agency or employer ask me for money to hire me?
info.contract_pay.fees.body: No. An authorised placement agency and an authorised employer may not ask you for commissions, fees, guarantees or deposits. The agency is paid only by the employer. Recruitment companies in your home country can charge you only within the limits of your country’s law. If an agency or employer in Romania asks you for money to hire you, do not pay: the law forbids it.
info.contract_pay.fees.step1: Do not pay money for a job.
info.contract_pay.fees.step2: If you have already paid, keep the proof: receipts, transfers, messages.
info.contract_pay.fees.step3: Complain to the Labour Inspection. If you are threatened, call 112.
info.contract_pay.costs_who_pays.title: Who pays for the visa, travel and accommodation?
info.contract_pay.costs_who_pays.body: As a rule, the law says that you pay for the visa, travel to Romania, transport inside Romania and accommodation. The employer can take over these costs if this is written in the job offer. The contract must clearly show what the employer pays, what you pay and which fees you owe to the Romanian authorities. The long-stay visa fee is 300 euros.
info.contract_pay.costs_who_pays.step1: Before you leave your country, read the job offer and check who pays for travel and accommodation.
info.contract_pay.costs_who_pays.step2: Keep receipts for everything you pay.
info.work_time.title: Working hours and conditions
info.work_time.hours.title: How many hours can I work?
info.work_time.hours.body: Normal working time is 8 hours a day and 40 hours a week. Including overtime, you cannot work more than 48 hours a week (on average, over a period of 4 months). Between two working days you have the right to at least 12 hours of rest in a row. Working 10–12 hour days, one after another, without rest is illegal.
info.work_time.hours.step1: Write down every day the time you start and finish work.
info.work_time.hours.step2: Take photos of the timesheet or of messages about your schedule.
info.work_time.hours.step3: If you work longer, you can complain to the Labour Inspection.
info.work_time.overtime.title: Overtime: do I have to do it? How is it paid?
info.work_time.overtime.body: Hours worked beyond your normal schedule are overtime. Your employer cannot make you work overtime without your agreement, except in cases of force majeure or urgent work to prevent or deal with an accident. Overtime is compensated with paid time off within the next 90 days. If you do not get time off, your employer must pay you an extra of at least 75% of your basic salary.
info.work_time.overtime.step1: Write down your overtime hours and keep evidence.
info.work_time.overtime.step2: Check on your payslip whether you got time off or extra pay.
info.work_time.overtime.step3: If you are threatened for refusing overtime, keep the messages and ask for help.
info.work_time.rest_leave.title: Do I have the right to breaks, days off and holidays?
info.work_time.rest_leave.body: Yes. If you work more than 6 hours a day, you have the right to a meal break. You have the right to 48 hours off in a row every week, usually Saturday and Sunday. You also have the right to paid annual leave of at least 20 working days a year.
info.work_time.rest_leave.step1: Check in your contract how many days of leave you have.
info.work_time.rest_leave.step2: Ask for leave in writing and keep the answer.
info.work_time.safety.title: What must my employer do for my safety?
info.work_time.safety.body: Your employer must train you on health and safety at work in a language you understand. They must give you the protective equipment you need, for example a helmet or gloves. You have the right to safety and health at work.
info.work_time.safety.step1: Ask for training and protective equipment before you start work.
info.work_time.safety.step2: If you are in immediate danger, get to safety and call 112.
info.work_time.safety.step3: Take photos of the dangerous place and complain to the Labour Inspection.
info.work_time.language_course.title: Do I have the right to a Romanian language course?
info.work_time.language_course.body: Yes. Under the new law, your employer must provide a Romanian language course, with information about life and culture in Romania. The course lasts at least 6 months from when you start work and has at least 6 hours a week. The employer pays for the course. Note: if you leave on your own initiative before 6 months, the employer can ask you to pay back the money spent on the course.
info.work_time.language_course.step1: Ask your employer when the course starts.
info.work_time.language_course.step2: If there is no course after you start work, you can complain to the Labour Inspection.
info.work_time.second_job.title: Can I also work for a second employer?
info.work_time.second_job.body: Yes, but with limits. If you have a residence permit for work and a full-time contract, you can work for another employer only with a part-time contract of at most 4 hours a day. The second job must also be in an occupation on the list of shortage occupations. Working without a contract is illegal.
info.work_time.second_job.step1: Ask for a written contract from the second employer too.
info.work_time.second_job.step2: Check that you are registered in REGES with the second employer as well.
info.documents.title: My documents
info.documents.passport_kept.title: Can my employer take my passport or residence permit?
info.documents.passport_kept.body: No. You must always carry your residence permit and you are not allowed to give it to anyone else. Your employer may only keep a copy of your passport or permit. If someone takes your documents and does not give them back, this can be a sign of exploitation.
info.documents.passport_kept.step1: Do not hand over original documents. Give only copies.
info.documents.passport_kept.step2: If they have been taken, ask for them back in writing (for example, on WhatsApp) and keep the message.
info.documents.passport_kept.step3: If they do not give them back, tell the General Inspectorate for Immigration in your county or the Police. If you are in danger, call 112.
info.documents.residence_permit.title: What is the residence permit and how long is it valid?
info.documents.residence_permit.body: You enter Romania with a long-stay visa for work. Then you get the single permit: your residence and work permit. It shows who you are, where you live and that you have the right to stay. The permit is granted for the length of your employment contract, but for at most 2 years. To extend it, you need a full-time contract and a salary at least equal to the gross minimum wage. Different rules apply to seasonal workers.
info.documents.residence_permit.step1: Write down the expiry date of your permit.
info.documents.residence_permit.step2: Ask your employer or agency to submit the extension application in good time.
info.documents.residence_permit.step3: After approval, book an appointment at Immigration within 10 days for your new permit.
info.change_job.title: Changing jobs
info.change_job.first_6_months.title: Can I leave my employer in the first 6 months?
info.change_job.first_6_months.body: In the first 6 months from when you started work in Romania (the date in REGES), you cannot resign to go to another employer. The 6 months are counted only once, from your first job in Romania, and do not start again when you change employer. Exception: if the employer seriously breaks the contract or your rights, for example does not pay your salary. The serious breach must be proven, and this can take time. The contract can still end earlier if the employer dismisses you or if you both agree (by mutual agreement).
info.change_job.first_6_months.step1: Keep evidence: contract, payslips, messages, photos, notes with dates.
info.change_job.first_6_months.step2: Complain to the Labour Inspection and keep the registration number.
info.change_job.first_6_months.step3: You can ask your employer, in writing, to end the contract by mutual agreement.
info.change_job.first_6_months.step4: Ask the foundation or another NGO for advice before you leave.
info.change_job.resignation.title: How do I resign correctly after the first 6 months?
info.change_job.resignation.body: You resign in writing and you do not have to give a reason. The employer must register your resignation. The contract ends after the notice period in your contract, which is at most 20 working days for most workers. If the employer does not respect its obligations under the contract, you can resign without notice. After the end of your contract is registered, you have at most 90 days to find another job (or less, if your permit expires earlier). If you came through an agency, for up to 2 years you change employer only through the same agency.
info.change_job.resignation.step1: Write your resignation, sign it and keep a copy with a registration number or date.
info.change_job.resignation.step2: If the employer refuses to register it, send it by email or post and keep the proof.
info.change_job.resignation.step3: Ask for the decision ending your contract.
info.change_job.mutual_agreement.title: What does ending the contract by “mutual agreement” mean?
info.change_job.mutual_agreement.body: You and your employer agree to end the contract on a certain date. You can ask for this at any time, even in the first 6 months. The employer does not have to accept. If they accept, you receive the decision ending the contract and you can look for another employer within the 90 days.
info.change_job.mutual_agreement.step1: Send the request in writing: by email, on WhatsApp or on paper with a registration number.
info.change_job.mutual_agreement.step2: Ask for the decision ending the contract and keep a copy.
info.change_job.mutual_agreement.step3: Check that the end of the contract appears in REGES.
info.change_job.release_letter.title: Do I still need an “acord” or release letter?
info.change_job.release_letter.body: No. The old rules on employing foreigners were repealed, and the employer’s “acord” for changing jobs no longer exists. You only need the document that ended your contract (the termination decision). Your new employer or the agency then submits a single application on WorkinRomania.gov.ro.
info.change_job.release_letter.step1: Keep the decision ending your contract.
info.change_job.release_letter.step2: If someone asks you for money for an “acord”, do not pay.
info.change_job.repay_costs.title: If I leave early, do I have to pay money back?
info.change_job.repay_costs.body: Possibly. If you leave on your own initiative before 6 months, without a serious breach by the employer, the employer can ask you to pay back the money spent on the Romanian course, accommodation and transport. This rule applies only if you do not respect the 6-month period.
info.change_job.repay_costs.step1: Before you leave, check your start date in REGES.
info.change_job.repay_costs.step2: Ask in writing for the list of costs the employer says it paid.
info.change_job.repay_costs.step3: If you disagree, ask the foundation or another NGO for advice.
info.change_job.agency_2_years.title: I came through an agency. Can I change employer?
info.change_job.agency_2_years.body: Yes, but with rules. After the first 6 months and until 2 years from when you started work in Romania, you can change employer only through the agency with which you signed the placement contract. If the agency has lost its authorisation, you can change employer in another way. The 6-month and 2-year periods are counted from your first job in Romania and do not start again when you change employer. After 2 years you can go through any authorised agency or to an authorised employer.
info.change_job.agency_2_years.step1: Talk to the agency and ask for job offers in writing.
info.change_job.old_law_workers.title: I came to Romania before the new law. Which rules apply to me?
info.change_job.old_law_workers.body: If you got your right of residence for work under the old law, since 8 August 2026 you can change employer through the new procedure: your new employer submits a single application on WorkinRomania.gov.ro. The new employer can hire you directly, without an agency, within a limit on the number of foreign workers. If you entered Romania with a visa granted under the old law, the first extension of your permit follows the old rules. The 6-month period in which you cannot leave on your own initiative is counted from when you started work in Romania, not from each employer.
info.change_job.old_law_workers.step1: Keep the termination decision from your old employer.
info.change_job.old_law_workers.step2: Ask your new employer for proof that it is listed on WorkinRomania.gov.ro.
info.change_job.old_law_workers.step3: Check your permit’s expiry date and the 90-day deadline.
info.job_loss.title: If I lose my job
info.job_loss.how_long_stay.title: How long can I stay in Romania without a job?
info.job_loss.how_long_stay.body: If your contract ends before your permit expires, you keep the right to stay for at most 90 days from when the end of the contract is registered. If your permit expires earlier, your right to stay ends on the expiry date. If you receive unemployment benefit, you can stay for as long as you receive it. Example: your permit expires on 3 June and the 90 days end on 31 July. You only have until 3 June to have your new contract and single application ready.
info.job_loss.how_long_stay.step1: Write down two dates: the day 90 days after the end of your contract was registered, and your permit’s expiry date. Your deadline is whichever comes first.
info.job_loss.how_long_stay.step2: Look for another job immediately and ask for the single application to be submitted before the deadline.
info.job_loss.how_long_stay.step3: If the deadline is close, ask the foundation or another NGO for help.
info.job_loss.agency_offers.title: What must the agency or employer do if I lose my job?
info.job_loss.agency_offers.body: If you came through an agency, the agency must give you at least two job offers in writing within the 90 days. If you refuse without a reason, the agency informs Immigration and ANOFM. If you worked directly for an authorised employer, the employer must put you in contact with a placement agency. If no new job is found, the agency or employer pays the cost of your return home.
info.job_loss.agency_offers.step1: Ask the agency for the offers in writing.
info.job_loss.agency_offers.step2: If you refuse an offer, write down the reason (for example, pay below the minimum wage or no accommodation).
info.job_loss.agency_offers.step3: If the agency does not help you, complain to the Labour Inspection or ask the foundation for help.
info.job_loss.after_deadline.title: What happens if I do not find another job in time?
info.job_loss.after_deadline.body: When the 90-day period ends or your permit expires, your stay becomes illegal without any further notice. You risk a fine and a return decision from the General Inspectorate for Immigration. If you lost your right to stay because of your employer (for example, they submitted the papers too late), ask a legal adviser for advice immediately.
info.job_loss.after_deadline.step1: Do not wait until the last day. Ask for help before the deadline.
info.job_loss.after_deadline.step2: If you received a return decision, read the question about it.
info.job_loss.return_decision.title: I received a return decision. What do I do?
info.job_loss.return_decision.body: The return decision is written in Romanian and in an international language. You can ask Immigration for a translation of its main parts into your language. You can challenge the decision at the court of appeal within 10 days from when it was communicated to you. As a rule, the challenge stops the return until the court decides. You can ask for state legal aid (a lawyer paid by the state), even if you do not meet the usual income conditions.
info.job_loss.return_decision.step1: Write down the date you received the decision. You have only 10 days.
info.job_loss.return_decision.step2: Immediately ask a lawyer, the foundation or another NGO for help.
info.job_loss.return_decision.step3: File the challenge at the court of appeal shown in the decision and ask for state legal aid.
info.complaints.title: Complaints and protection
info.complaints.where_complain.title: Where do I complain?
info.complaints.where_complain.body:
It depends on the problem:
• Labour Inspection (ITM): unpaid salary, working hours that are too long, no contract, dangerous conditions.
• General Inspectorate for Immigration (IGI): problems with your permit, documents taken by the employer.
• Police: violence, threats, being locked in or not allowed to leave.
• Prosecutor’s Office: criminal complaint for serious acts.
• ANITP (0800 800 678): human trafficking or forced labour.
• National Council for Combating Discrimination (CNCD): discrimination.
In an emergency, call 112.
info.complaints.where_complain.step1: Use “I have a problem” in the app to prepare your complaint and send it by email.
info.complaints.where_complain.step3: Ask for and keep the registration number.
info.complaints.registration_number.titl: What is a registration number? How soon will I get an answer?
info.complaints.registration_number.body: When you file a complaint with an institution, ask for a registration number. It contains a number and the date, for example: Nr. 23/03.07.2026. You receive it on paper or by email. The institution must answer you within 30 days from registration. This deadline can be extended by up to 15 days if the problem needs more investigation. Other deadlines apply in court and for some special requests.
info.complaints.registration_number.step: Ask for the registration number every time.
Keep it: you can use it to ask what happened to your complaint.
If you get no answer within 30 days, write again and mention the number.
info.complaints.evidence.title: What evidence should I keep?
info.complaints.evidence.body: Without evidence it is much harder to defend your rights with the authorities or in court. Keep everything that shows what happened: contracts, payslips, work schedules, messages, photos, recordings. Write down dates, names of people and what happened.
info.complaints.evidence.step1: Take photos of every document you sign.
info.complaints.evidence.step2: Save your messages (WhatsApp, SMS) and send a copy to someone you trust.
info.complaints.evidence.step3: You can attach photos directly to your complaint in the app.
info.complaints.retaliation.title: Can I be punished for making a complaint?
info.complaints.retaliation.body: No. The law forbids any unfavourable treatment (for example dismissal, lower pay or threats) as a reaction to a complaint to the authorities or because you asked for your rights. Your employer cannot threaten to cancel your visa or have you expelled because you complained. If this happens, you can complain about it too.
info.complaints.retaliation.step2: Complain to the Labour Inspection and say you were punished after your complaint.
info.complaints.workinromania_complaints: Can I complain on WorkinRomania.gov.ro? Who sees the complaint?

The law requires foreign workers to have access to confidential complaint procedures, including through the WorkinRomania.gov.ro platform. The platform is run by the Ministry of Internal Affairs, and the General Inspectorate for Immigration has access to its data. Keep this in mind when you choose where to complain.
If you are not sure where to complain, ask the foundation or another NGO for advice.
For work problems you can complain directly to the Labour Inspection.
info.complaints.discrimination.title: I am treated worse because I am a foreigner. What can I do?
info.complaints.discrimination.body: Discrimination at work is forbidden, including on grounds of citizenship, ethnicity, language or religion. You have the right to the same pay, the same schedule and the same conditions as Romanian workers doing the same work. Harassment and humiliation at work are also forbidden.
info.complaints.discrimination.step1: Write down what happened, when, and who was present.
info.complaints.discrimination.step2: Complain to the Labour Inspection or to the National Council for Combating Discrimination (CNCD).
info.complaints.union_strike.title: Do I have the right to join a union or go on strike?
info.complaints.union_strike.body: Yes. You have the right to join or set up a trade union and to take part in collective actions. Taking part in a strike is voluntary: nobody can force you to take part or not to take part. Your employer cannot dismiss you for being in a union or for lawfully taking part in a strike.
info.complaints.union_strike.step1: Ask your colleagues whether there is a union at your workplace.
info.complaints.union_strike.step2: You can contact a trade union confederation, for example Blocul Național Sindical (bns@bns.ro).
info.complaints.trafficking.title: I think I am a victim of human trafficking or forced labour. What do I do?
info.complaints.trafficking.body: Warning signs: your documents were taken, you are not allowed to leave, you are threatened, you work to pay off a debt that keeps growing, or you are not paid. Victims of human trafficking have the right to protection and assistance. A foreign victim of trafficking can get a recovery and reflection period of up to 90 days and, under certain conditions, the right to stay in Romania.
info.complaints.trafficking.step1: If you are in danger, call 112.
info.complaints.trafficking.step2: Call the ANITP helpline 0800 800 678 (free; not available 24/7).
info.complaints.trafficking.step3: You can also contact organisations that help victims: eLiberare (info@eliberare.com) or ADPARE (adpare@adpare.eu).
info.health_family.title: Health and family
info.health_family.health.title: Do I have health insurance? How do I see a doctor?
info.health_family.health.body: If you work legally, with a contract, you are insured in the public health system: the health contribution (10%) is deducted from your salary. As an insured person you can register with a family doctor. To see a specialist or to get free or cheaper tests, you need a referral (bilet de trimitere) from your family doctor.
info.health_family.health.step1: After you get your residence permit, register with a family doctor near your home.
info.health_family.health.step2: Ask for a referral before you go to a specialist.
info.health_family.family.title: Can I bring my family to Romania?
info.health_family.family.body: Yes, if you have a residence permit valid for at least one year. You can apply for family reunification for your husband or wife and for your unmarried minor children. You need suitable housing, health insurance and money: in addition to what you need for yourself, the gross minimum wage for 3 months for each family member. The application is submitted to Immigration and decided within at most 3 months. If it is approved, your family has 60 days to take the approval to the Romanian embassy and apply for a visa. Family members with a family reunification permit can work in Romania, in occupations on the list of shortage occupations.
info.health_family.family.step1: Prepare the documents: marriage or birth certificate, proof of housing, money and insurance.
info.health_family.family.step2: Submit the application to Immigration in the county where you live.
info.health_family.family.step3: Send the approval to your family. They take it to the embassy within 60 days.
